def transform(grid):
    # Tiles separated by 1-cell colored dividers; repeat the pattern from first tile
    # into each other region along both axes, preserving divider lines.
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # For this task, identify rows/columns containing uniform divider color 4.
    div=4
    dr=[r for r,row in enumerate(grid) if all(x==div for x in row)]
    dc=[c for c in range(w) if all(grid[r][c]==div for r in range(h))]
    # Find the fundamental tile size from first divider boundaries, replicate source tile.
    rs=[-1]+dr+[h]
    cs=[-1]+dc+[w]
    # The source is the upper-left region; repeat its non-background marks periodically
    out=[row[:] for row in grid]
    # Source pattern within first block; background is most common value there.
    r0,r1=0,dr[0] if dr else h
    c0,c1=0,dc[0] if dc else w
    tile=[row[c0:c1] for row in grid[r0:r1]]
    from collections import Counter
    bg=Counter(x for row in tile for x in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    th,tw=len(tile),len(tile[0])
    for r in range(h):
      for c in range(w):
        if grid[r][c]==div: continue
        if r<r1 and c<c1: continue
        tr=(r-r1-1)%th if r>=r1 else r%th
        tc=(c-c1-1)%tw if c>=c1 else c%tw
        # Repeat first tile's pattern, but leave blank where tile blank.
        v=tile[tr][tc]
        if v!=bg: out[r][c]=v
    return out
PY
